notes: Core Nano is a network-only Q-SYS AV&C processor with no onboard analog audio I/O; all audio/video is carried over the two Gigabit Ethernet ports (Q-LAN/AES67/Dante/VoIP). Listed as 1U half-width (occupies half a standard rack width at 1U height); rackUnits set to 1 to reflect height. RS232 x2 ports use a 3-position 3.5mm captive/euroblock-style connector (mapped to euroblock, the closest listed connector; QSC uses TX/RX/GND terminals per port). USB-C port is multi-function (USB 3.1 host, DisplayPort alt-mode, or USB device port when USB-B is idle) — modeled as bidirectional usb-c graded usb-5g (USB 3.1 Gen1/"3.0" class transfer rate per QSC's own USB 3.0/3.1 labeling; note QSC datasheet's USB Inputs & Outputs table separately states 16-bit/8x8/48kHz audio over USB, which is a protocol-level spec not a physical port). USB-B port is a dedicated USB 3.0 device port. Four USB-A host ports total, confirmed via official Q-SYS Help hardware pages (grouped as two pairs on the rear panel; QSC does not give each an individual numeric label, so they are named USB A1-A4 here for disambiguation). LAN A and LAN B are both RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet (1000 Mbps) - LAN A primary, LAN B backup/failover, both used for Q-LAN/AES67/Dante/VoIP/control traffic. AC power inlet is IEC 60320 C14, universal 100-240V 50/60Hz auto-switching (mapped to connector id "iec" as the closest match to C13/C14 family per instructions). Sources cross-checked: QSC/Q-SYS official spec sheet PDF (qsys.com) and Q-SYS Help hardware documentation (help.qsys.com, multiple version pages consistent).
